title: Quantum beyond computing
summary: Quantum sensing with diamond defects, hyperpolarised MRI of tumour metabolism, the proton-tunnelling hypothesis of mutation — and how to write about “quantum” without feeding pseudoscience.

shots.title:
Quantum beyond
computing.
shots.subtitle: Sensors already in the clinic, hypotheses still in theory.
shots.narration: Not all quantum oncology is computing. Some of it is measurement, already working in patients. Some of it is biology, still hypothesis. Knowing the difference keeps your papers credible.

shots.text: **Quantum sensing**: using quantum systems — such as the spin states of atomic defects — to measure physical quantities.
shots.narration: Quantum sensing means using quantum systems, properties or phenomena — such as the spin states of single atomic defects — to measure physical quantities with high sensitivity.

shots.text: **Nitrogen-vacancy centres** in diamond: stable, photostable, low-toxicity — nanoscale sensors of magnetic and electric fields.
shots.narration: The workhorse is the nitrogen-vacancy centre in diamond: a defect that is stable, photostable and low in toxicity, whose spin state senses magnetic and electric fields at the nanoscale.

shots.label: lower detection limit than gold nanoparticles in a lateral-flow test
shots.context: microwave-modulated fluorescent nanodiamonds · model assay; single-copy HIV-1 RNA with amplification
shots.narration: In 2020, fluorescent nanodiamonds modulated with microwaves made a lateral-flow test a hundred thousand times more sensitive than gold nanoparticles in a model assay, and detected single copies of HIV RNA with a ten-minute amplification step.

shots.label: signal-to-noise gain from dissolution hyperpolarisation in NMR
shots.narration: Hyperpolarisation works on nuclear spins. Polarising a molecule before injecting it can raise the magnetic resonance signal more than ten-thousand-fold.

shots.text: 2013: first-in-human hyperpolarised **pyruvate MRI** — **31** men with prostate cancer; more **lactate** where the cancer was.
shots.narration: In 2013 the first study in humans imaged thirty-one men with prostate cancer using hyperpolarised pyruvate. It was safe, and it showed more lactate, relative to pyruvate, in regions of biopsy-proven cancer — the Warburg effect, imaged.

shots.text: 1963: could protons **tunnelling** across DNA base pairs create rare forms that cause **mutations**?
shots.narration: Now quantum biology. In 1963 Per-Olov Löwdin proposed that protons tunnelling along the hydrogen bonds of DNA could create rare base forms — tautomers — that cause mutations.

shots.text: A 2022 model: tunnelling dominates, tautomer occupation **1.73 × 10⁻⁴** — but **no one has measured** its share of real mutations.
shots.narration: A 2022 open-quantum-systems model found tunnelling dominates proton transfer in guanine–cytosine pairs, with a tautomer occupation of one point seven three in ten thousand. But it is theory: whether these tautomers survive replication, and how many real mutations they cause, has not been measured.

shots.text: Treat quantum-biology claims about cancer as **hypotheses** until they are **measured in cells**.
shots.narration: So treat quantum-biology claims about cancer as hypotheses until they are measured in cells. They make good theory papers; they are not yet facts about tumours.

shots.text: Replacing treatment with alternative medicine: **2.5×** the risk of death. The word “quantum” is often the product.
shots.narration: And the dark side. Patients who replaced conventional treatment with alternative medicine had two and a half times the risk of death. “Quantum” is a favourite word on those products. Write precisely, so your work cannot be borrowed for them.

steps.title: How established is it?
steps.brief: Sort each claim by the strongest evidence behind it.

cards.text: Hyperpolarised pyruvate MRI shows high lactate in prostate tumours
Nanodiamond labels make a lateral-flow test far more sensitive
cards.why: Model assays plus a clinical plasma sample — a long way from routine use.

cards.text: Proton tunnelling causes a measurable share of cancer mutations
G–C base pairs reach tautomeric equilibrium fast through tunnelling
cards.why: A theoretical result from a 2022 model.
No mechanism, no evidence, and a real risk to patients who delay treatment.

questions.prompt: What did the first-in-human hyperpolarised pyruvate study find in prostate cancer?
options: Elevated lactate-to-pyruvate ratios in biopsy-proven cancer
questions.explain: Safe, and more lactate where the cancer was.

questions.prompt: Why is the 2022 proton-tunnelling result marked “contested”?
options: It is a theoretical model; its contribution to real mutation rates has not been measured
questions.explain: A strong theory paper, not yet a measured fact about cells.

options: Reading the spin of a nitrogen-vacancy centre to measure a magnetic field
questions.explain: Sensing uses quantum states to measure; computing uses them to calculate.
